conclusion: The opposite reading is that this run moved toward the markets on evidence that does not test the thing it was shaded for. Early-vote composition says who votes early. Ohio's polls have missed toward Republicans four cycles running, including Brown himself twice. Republicans have a 2-to-1 dollar edge in September Senate TV. conclusion: Cable will say Iowa's early vote shows Democrats surging. At 14 days out the Democratic share is exactly its 2022 level. Republicans are 4 points short, and Grassley won by 12 from a similar early mix.

The scheduled-task brief quoted Iowa's Democratic early-vote edge (53.8 vs 50.5) from the Oct 19 file. One day later the same-point comparison shows no Democratic edge (53.6 vs 53.6). The brief's caution about 2022 timing was correct.

The brief quoted Texas as a 57,342-ballot first day. The state app now shows 496,045 through Oct 20 (partial), including 419,343 in-person votes on Oct 19. The 57,342 figure predated the first in-person day.

The Iowa Secretary of State PDF the ev_more fetcher reads is dated Oct 16 (33,418 received), while UF's compilation is Oct 20 (93,169). The two series measure different things and should not be mixed.
The lock reported no fall Maine poll. Seven October Maine polls existed before the lock (Suffolk, Marist, WaPo-Schar and others). That was a retrieval gap at lock time.

The core model's appointee list (core_model.APPOINTED) named Ohio and Florida but not South Carolina, so Darline Graham, appointed July 13, carried an eight-point incumbency term the frozen rule reserves for elected incumbents. Fixed on 2026-10-28: the model's South Carolina fundamentals move from Graham +16.3 to Graham +8.3.
